newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK blue chips nudge ahead, China plays end strong.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips nudge ahead, China plays end strong.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips ended with only moderate gains on Wednesday as this week's rebound in prices began to slow, but China plays rallied amid a lack of interest in big cap stocks and strength in mainland markets.
The Hang Seng Index rose 28.11 points, or 0.23 percent, to 12,426.68 after climbing to an early session high of 12,451.46.
"I think the market is being pushed up by traders who had perceived the floor at 12,000," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"However, we are running into a little bit of a brick wall with regard to the blue chips given that there is strong resistance at 12,400 to 12,500."
Turnover on Wednesday was HK$6.66 billion compared with HK$6.85 billion on Tuesday.

Brokers said concerns about higher interest rates and fears of a correction in the local property market were keeping investors cautious, particularly after a 222.09 point rise in the Hang Seng Index so far this week.
Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities, said 12,500 points seemed to be a strong resistance level for the Hang Seng Index.
"It looks like the market will consolidate probably in a range of 12,200 to 12,500," he said.
But Wong said a rebound towards 12,700 to 12,750 was possible later. "Right now the (U.S.) dollar is very strong and this increases the attractiveness of dollar-based assets."
"Also the dollar is so strong that it looks like the Fed may not be willing to raise interest rates again. I think that the outlook possibly has improved."
The dollar/yen is at its highest level since August 1992.
Brokers said the main focus on Wednesday had been red-chip stocks.
"Red chips are obviously in vogue today. Ahead of June/July you will see these China shares go better," said Remington.

The H-share index surged 33.16 points, or 3.45 percent, to 995.63. Among the red chips, China Resources Enterprise Ltd rose HK$0.80 to HK$17.40 and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd gained HK$0.80 to HK$35.50.
Brokers said the firm tone on Chinese domestic markets had helped. The Shanghai A-share index rose 42.496 points to 1,349.527 and the Shenzhen A-share index gained 9.29 to 465.67.
Among the blue chips, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd fell HK$0.80 to HK$77.50 and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd slipped HK$0.25 to HK$64.75.
HSBC Holdings Plc gained HK$1.50 to HK$181.50.
